properties.natural_language: Before routing a URL request via EDGE-USER-REQUEST, the external web user must provide a well-formed URL matching one of the four standardized patterns: /block/*, /tx/*, /address/*, or /token/*
After URL parsing via ACTION-PARSE-URL-PATH, exactly one of the four request states must be reached: block, tx, address, or token identified
Every URL request must eventually reach STATE-PAGE-RENDERED or be rejected; no request may remain indefinitely in an intermediate state
Before fetching block data, the block identifier must be either a valid 0x-prefixed hex hash or a decimal integer height
After page rendering, the returned page via EDGE-RETURN-PAGE must correspond to the exact resource identified in the URL path
The blockchain data source queried for all fetch actions must be synchronized and accurate to prevent stale data display
Before redirect compatibility check via EDGE-RECEIVE-STANDARD-URL, the incoming request must use EIP-3091 standard URL format
After ACTION-CHECK-NATIVE-SUPPORT, exactly one path is taken: native route exists or redirect is required
After redirect generation, the HTTP redirect response must use status 301 or 302 and point to a valid internal URL that serves the same resource
Redirect chains must not introduce infinite loops; every redirect must terminate at a content-serving endpoint
Before processing any URL input at the security boundary via EDGE-UNTRUSTED-INPUT, the raw URL path must be treated as untrusted and subject to sanitization
After path format validation, invalid paths must be rejected and must not reach any data fetch or rendering action
No URL input may bypass both ACTION-VALIDATE-PATH-FORMAT and ACTION-VALIDATE-IDENTIFIER; all inputs must pass both validations to reach STATE-INPUT-VALIDATED
Before executing a PUSH operation, sufficient gas must be available (GAS_BASE for PUSH0, GAS_VERY_LOW for PUSH1-32) and the stack must have fewer than 1024 items
After PUSH completes, the stack height must increase by exactly 1 and the program counter must advance by 1 + N where N is the number of immediate bytes
The pushed value must exactly match the big-endian interpretation of the N bytes read from bytecode; bytecode must be immutable during execution
Before POP execution, the stack must have at least one item (stack height >= 1) and GAS_BASE gas must be available
After POP completes, the stack height must decrease by exactly 1 and the value previously at the top must be discarded
POP must not modify any stack values other than removing the top item; all remaining items must preserve their relative ordering
Before DUPn execution, the stack must have at least n items (item_number < len(stack)) and GAS_VERY_LOW gas must be available
After successful DUP, the stack height must increase by 1 and the new top must equal the value previously at position n
When stack underflow is detected, execution must halt with StackUnderflowError and no stack modification must occur
The DUP operation must not modify the original value at position n; it must only add a copy at the top
Before SWAPn execution, the stack must have at least n+1 items (item_number < len(stack)) and GAS_VERY_LOW gas must be available
After successful SWAP, the value at position 0 and position n must be exchanged, with stack height unchanged
When SWAP underflow is detected, execution must halt with StackUnderflowError and no stack modification must occur
Gas is always charged before any stack operation logic executes, regardless of whether the operation succeeds or fails with underflow
Before processing a chain switch request via EDGE-DAPP-REQUEST, the dApp must provide a valid 0x-prefixed EIP-155 chainId
Before switching chains, the wallet must be in STATE-WALLET-ON-CHAIN-A with an active connection to the current chain
After user approval, the wallet must transition to STATE-WALLET-ON-CHAIN-B with the requested chainId active for the current session
After user rejection, the wallet must return error code 4001 to the dApp and remain on the original chain
No chain switch may occur without explicit user confirmation; the wallet must always prompt the user via ACTION-PROMPT-USER-SWITCH or ACTION-PROMPT-USER-ADD
Before RPC URL validation, the URL must pass sanitization to prevent injection attacks, SSRF via private IP ranges, and protocol enforcement (HTTPS required)
After calling eth_chainId on the RPC endpoint, the returned chainId must match the chainId in the original request; mismatches must cause rejection
Malformed URLs must always be rejected at the sanitization step and never reach the net_version or eth_chainId RPC calls
Before SSRF detection via EDGE-MALICIOUS-INPUT, the system must classify incoming requests from untrusted dApps as potentially malicious
After SSRF detection finds an internal target URL, the request must be immediately blocked without any outgoing network call
After phishing detection identifies a chain name mismatch, the user must be warned via ACTION-WARN-USER before any further processing
All chain switch requests from external dApps must pass through both SSRF detection and chain list verification before reaching the user
Before receiving builder bids via EDGE-BID-RECEIVED, the proposer must be assigned to a slot and subscribed to the execution_payload_bid gossip topic
After bid validation, only bids that pass builder balance coverage, parent hash match, and signature verification may be selected
After block construction, the signed beacon block must contain both the selected builder bid and aggregated payload attestations (up to MAX_PAYLOAD_ATTESTATIONS)
Proposer preferences broadcasting is optional (MAY); the block proposal flow must succeed regardless of whether preferences were published
Before creating an attestation, the validator must have reached ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS_GLOAS (25% of slot) and must check fork-choice for parent payload presence
After creating an attestation, data.index must be set to 0 (absent) or 1 (present) based on parent payload status in fork-choice
Before creating a payload attestation message, the PTC member must be assigned via get_ptc_assignment and must wait until 75% of the slot
After PTC attestation creation, the PayloadAttestationMessage must be broadcast to the network signaling payload timeliness
Before accepting any builder bid from the untrusted external builder via EDGE-BID-FROM-BUILDER, the bid must be treated as untrusted and enter STATE-BID-RECEIVED-UNTRUSTED
After all three validation steps (balance, parent hash, signature), the bid must transition to STATE-BID-TRUSTED; failure at any step must reject the bid
Builder bid validation must follow strict sequential order: balance check, then parent hash verification, then signature verification; no step may be skipped
If no proposer preferences were broadcast, the proposer signals unwillingness to accept trustless builder bids; STATE-NO-PREFERENCES-BROADCAST must be respected
Before processing an uncle block RPC request via EDGE-CLIENT-SUBMITS-REQUEST, the client must provide valid block hash and uncle index parameters
After fork state determination, exactly one path is taken: pre-EIP-1559 (baseFee omitted) or post-EIP-1559 (baseFee included)
After response construction, the response returned to the client via EDGE-RETURN-RESPONSE must include baseFee only for post-EIP-1559 blocks
The baseFee value in post-EIP-1559 responses must be the actual consensus-validated baseFee from the block header, never a computed or estimated value
Before baseFee field validation, uncle block data must be successfully retrieved from storage
After validation determines baseFee is required, the value must be extracted from the actual uncle block header via ACTION-EXTRACT-BASEFEE-VALUE
The fork state determination must be consistent across all client implementations using the same EIP-1559 activation block configuration
Before an EIP enters evaluation via EDGE-SUBMIT-PROPOSAL, the EIP author must submit a complete specification via the external entity boundary
After evaluation, an EIP must transition to either STATE-EIP-CONSIDERED (passes initial review) or be rejected; no EIP may remain indefinitely in STATE-EIP-PROPOSED
After consideration, an EIP must reach either STATE-EIP-SCHEDULED or STATE-EIP-DECLINED; these are terminal states for the upgrade cycle
The EIP lifecycle must follow strict ordering: Proposed -> Considered -> (Scheduled | Declined); no backward transitions are allowed
Before configuring activation times via EDGE-CLIENT-TEAMS-DECIDE, client teams must have agreed on activation timestamps through coordination
After activation configuration, testnets (Sepolia, Holesky) must be activated before mainnet to enable testing
Activation timestamps, once configured, must be consistently applied across all client implementations for a given network
Before processing a KZG commitment via EDGE-RECEIVE-COMMITMENT, the blob transaction must provide a valid 48-byte KZG commitment
After versioned hash creation, the result must be exactly 32 bytes with 0x01 as the first byte followed by 31 bytes of the SHA256 hash
The kzg_commitment_to_versioned_hash function must be deterministic: the same 48-byte input must always produce the same 32-byte versioned hash
Before G1 point validation via EDGE-RECEIVE-BYTES48, the untrusted 48-byte input must be received and classified as untrusted
After G1 point validation, the point must be either accepted as valid (including infinity case) or rejected as invalid; no intermediate state is allowed
Before BLS modulus check via EDGE-RECEIVE-BYTES32, the untrusted 32-byte field element must be received from an external source
After BLS modulus check, values >= BLS modulus must be rejected; only values strictly less than the modulus are valid field elements
The point at infinity (0xc0 + 47 zero bytes) must always be accepted as a valid G1 point without further BLS verification
Before KZG proof verification via EDGE-RECEIVE-PROOF-INPUTS, all four inputs (commitment 48B, z 32B, y 32B, proof 48B) must be provided with correct lengths
After pairing check, the proof is valid if and only if the BLS12-381 pairing equals FQ12.one(); any other result means the proof is invalid
The trusted setup parameter KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL_1 must be used correctly and must not be compromised; all proof security depends on this
Both G1 and G2 computations must complete before the pairing check can execute; they may run in parallel but both results are required
After input length validation and type conversion, all cryptographic types must be valid before G1/G2 computations begin
Before base fee calculation, parent block's gas_used, gas_limit, and base_fee_per_gas must all be available and valid
After comparing usage to target, exactly one of three states must be reached: at target, above target, or below target
The base fee change per block must not exceed 12.5% (1/8) in either direction; this rate limit prevents fee manipulation by block producers
When usage exactly equals target, the base fee must remain unchanged (no increase or decrease)
Before transaction type detection via EDGE-EXT-TX-IN, the raw transaction bytes must be received from the external transaction submitter
After type detection, exactly one of three types must be identified: legacy (no prefix), access list (0x01), or fee market (0x02)
For EIP-1559 transactions, the effective gas price must be calculated as min(max_priority_fee, max_fee - base_fee) + base_fee
All transaction types must ultimately reach STATE-TX-DECODED with a valid effective gas price; no transaction may complete decoding without a computed effective price
Before access list processing, the transaction must include a non-empty access_list with declared addresses and storage keys
After access list processing, all declared addresses must be marked warm and all declared storage keys must be marked warm for reduced access costs
Access list gas cost must be exactly: (address_count * 2400) + (storage_key_count * 1900), added to TX_BASE_COST and data costs
Before gas refund calculation, transaction execution must be complete with a valid refund counter from SSTORE operations
After refund calculation, the actual refund must not exceed 20% of gas consumed (London's reduced cap from 50%)
After refund completion, the sender must receive exactly (gas_limit - effective_gas_used) * effective_gas_price back to their account
The effective gas used must always be: gas_consumed - min(refund_counter, gas_consumed * 20%); this formula must be applied consistently
Before computing custody groups, the node must have joined the network with a known node-id
After custody computation, the node must have exactly CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT (4) unique custody groups assigned deterministically from node-id
After column computation, each custody group maps to specific columns via: NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS * i + custody_group
After subscribing to gossip subnets, the node must begin receiving DataColumnSidecars for all assigned columns
Custody group assignment must be deterministic: the same node-id must always produce the same set of custody groups across all nodes in the network
Before data recovery, the node must have at least 50% (64 of 128) columns available for Reed-Solomon reconstruction
After successful recovery, all 128 columns must be reconstructed for every blob in the block, achieving full data availability
After full recovery, reconstructed data must be cross-seeded to the network before the node can attest to data availability
Recovery must use polynomial interpolation (recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs) per blob row, maintaining cryptographic integrity of reconstructed cells
Before sampling, a new slot must have started with a proposed block requiring data availability verification
After KZG proof verification for all sampled columns, sampling passes only if ALL proofs are valid; any single failure causes sampling to fail
For columns not available via gossip, the node must fall back to direct req/resp queries to custody peers before concluding unavailability
Before light client header construction, a signed beacon block must be available and well-formed
After fork epoch check, Capella-era blocks must produce headers with execution payload data and Merkle proofs, while pre-Capella blocks produce empty execution headers
The Merkle branch in the light client header must be a valid proof of the execution payload's inclusion in the beacon block body
Before execution payload proof validation, the light client must have received a header and have access to the correct beacon block body root from a trusted source
After Merkle branch verification, the proof must either be valid (matches beacon block body root) or invalid (mismatch); invalid proofs must cause header rejection
Light clients must never accept execution payload headers that fail Merkle branch verification, regardless of other header validity indicators
